correctness.rationale: One-agent S5 with n>=1 finite propositional atoms, XOR, negation and constants but no conjunction: every propositional truth value is affine over F2. For a pointed class, a is its distinguished valuation, H=aff(X) of all class valuation vectors. Affine functions vanish on X iff on H. Structural induction, including nested Box/Diamond, shows each formula evaluates as L_phi(a) xor c_phi(H), since modalities of affine operands are constant on the class and depend only on H. Different a are separated by an atom; different H with same a by Diamond of an affine linear equation vanishing on one H but not other (choose direction appropriately). A d-dimensional H has an affine basis of d+1 valuation points including a, and fewer accessible worlds cannot span H; optimal size d+1 and worst-case n+1. For each d, G_2(n,d) linear subspaces, 2^(n-d) translates, 2^d possible a, total pointed theories 2^n sum_d G_2(n,d). Exact independent n=1,2,3 computations give 4,20,128, matching the proof; no claim for full Boolean languages or multiple agents.
residual_risks: Bounded independent tests do not prove any unbounded theorem; the written proof was reconstructed and tested against boundary assumptions.

originality.rationale: Krebs–Meier's affine S5 satisfiability hardness principally uses two accessibility relations; hardness does not classify one-agent logical equivalence or minimum finite models. Modal Fragments 2026 investigates restricted Boolean bases and basis-sensitive bisimulation but does not provide this precise S5 affine-hull iff and Gaussian pointed-type census. General unrestricted Boolean S5 normal forms distinguish exact reachable valuation sets X, not merely their affine spans; therefore they do not directly give the sharp XOR quotient/compression formula. Similar two-agent properization findings are logically separate.
residual_risks: A logically equivalent affine-fragment theorem may exist in unindexed modal-logic literature.
One equivalence relation and finite n are essential; inclusion of conjunction distinguishes raw reachable valuation sets even when affine hull agrees.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete, nontrivial semantic invariant for a natural Boolean clone in epistemic modal logic, with sharp model compression and an exact all-n counting formula. It explicates the qualitative change from one to two agents and from affine to full Boolean syntax and is a useful precise example for basis-restricted modal expressivity.
residual_risks: Exact finite/general value rests on intrinsic mathematical motivation, not reproducibility alone.
